decision: Absorb the konjo-* skill family into kiban's global plugins/konjo/skills/ plane instead of keeping a per-repo copy.
rationale: lopi's docs/LOOP_ENGINEERING_ROADMAP.md asserted four capability gaps already closed on main because konjo-ship's checklist named no file that would ever surface it; the per-repo copy plane is what let it decay unnoticed.
alternatives_considered: keep the per-repo plane and build a sync mechanism
hand-edit lopi/miru now
author: wes

decision: Add Konjo-Doc-Verified as a fourth record-and-check trailer, reusing oneway.make_trailer/find_trailer and the existing fingerprint scheme.
rationale: a decays: state doc with no verified-against stamp is a hard FAIL; the trailer needed a home in the same family as Konjo-Acknowledged-Oneway and Konjo-Prove-Merge rather than inventing a fourth format.
alternatives_considered: invent a new ad hoc trailer format
author: wes

decision: Make review incompleteness block the merge instead of passing silently.
rationale: CLIBackend.dispatch funneled TimeoutExpired, OSError, and a non-zero CLI exit into a return value the parser reads as zero findings, so a specialist that never completed was indistinguishable from a clean review.
alternatives_considered: WARN-only signal on incomplete review
author: wes

decision: Retry a failed review specialist once before hard-blocking, rather than blocking immediately on first failure.
rationale: a transient network blip should not cost the same as a specialist that is actually broken, or operators will start treating every INCOMPLETE as noise.
alternatives_considered: immediate block on first failure
multi-run self-consistency
author: wes

decision: Write KONJO_FORWARD.md for real instead of continuing to cite it as an already-established doc.
rationale: the birth-defect proposal and this sprint's own brief quoted exact sentences from a doc that did not exist in the repo; the gap needed recording, not papering over.
alternatives_considered: quietly author it with no note that it was previously missing
author: wes

decision: Author profiles/lopi.yml documenting what lopi's CI already enforces, without rebuilding lopi's own enforcement.
rationale: nine of lopi's real CI checks stay repo-native by design; this phase connects the pilot, it does not take over lopi's CI.
alternatives_considered: migrate lopi's checks into konjo-gates wholesale
author: wes

decision: Build konjo-threat / gate_threat_model as a third record-and-check pair, and add security_globs as a new permanent profile field.
rationale: brief-time classification against a fixed eight-class trust-boundary taxonomy, matching konjo-oneway/konjo-prove's existing shape.
alternatives_considered: fold threat classification into the existing oneway mechanism instead of a new pair
author: wes

decision: Add evals/gen_fixtures/ and konjo-eval gen as a new, report-only fixture generation path.
rationale: grows the eval corpus's shape without a blocking gate; distinct fixture shape from the hand-authored ones, so it needed its own CI job.
alternatives_considered: extend the existing hand-authored fixture path instead of a new one
author: wes

decision: Convert lopi's four sprint-cited security lines through konjo-learn instead of leaving them as prose citations.
rationale: confirmed by running the guardrail for real -- only security.md carried any Sprint S\d+ citations, and all four found a home.
alternatives_considered: leave the citations as plain prose, uningested
author: wes

decision: Author profiles/squish.yml and profiles/vectro.yml promote/keep/delete tables without rebuilding either repo's CI.
rationale: matches Lopi-Gate-Reconciliation-1's own non-goal-respecting shape: connect and record what exists, don't rebuild it.
alternatives_considered: rebuild squish's and vectro's CI while reconciling
author: wes

decision: Record that most of squish's and vectro's 'Wall 2' CI is decorative, without fixing it this phase.
rationale: read both repos' real konjo-gate.yml in full rather than trusting profiles/*.yml's existing declarations; a real finding neither the brief nor either repo's own CLAUDE.md had named.
alternatives_considered: silently fix the decorative CI while reconciling
author: wes

decision: Classify 4 more of the 8 defect taxonomy classes mechanically (3 to 7 of 8) in evals/genfixtures.py.
rationale: grew mechanical coverage without writing a fully new detector for most of it, per 'reuse before you build'.
alternatives_considered: write a bespoke detector for every remaining taxonomy class
author: wes

decision: Publish an honest null result: both tested context-reduction candidates measured null on real closed lopi work.
rationale: 2 tasks, 3 conditions, deliberately distinct from KT-14.1's tasks to avoid confounding incidental-defect reduction with explicit-fix-instruction following; the measurement itself caught a live classifier bug.
alternatives_considered: quietly shelve the null result and not publish it
author: wes

decision: Build lib/gen_runner.py + evals/gen_cassettes.py + konjo-eval genrun as the missing 'task in, diff out' measurement instrument.
rationale: konjo-headless/lib/headless.py was found to be a thin claude -p argv builder with no such loop; Phase 1 builds the loop as a consumer of lib.headless, not a replacement.
alternatives_considered: replace lib.headless outright instead of building a consumer on top
author: wes

decision: Instrument the review-pipeline plan's telemetry and backfill it against real history before writing any gate.
rationale: PF-1 corrected the plan on two tooling assumptions before any code was written.
alternatives_considered: build the gate first and instrument telemetry later
author: wes

decision: Ship the plan-artifact schema and the telemetry fields it feeds from kiban's side, leaving the Planner/Executor handoff itself to lopi's own sprint.
rationale: kiban's scope is the schema and telemetry wiring; the handoff and its kill-tests are recorded in lopi's own LEDGER.md.
alternatives_considered: implement the Planner/Executor handoff inside kiban itself
author: wes

decision: Ship the mutation-feedback formatter (section 2) this phase; defer sections 1, 3, and 4 until the PF-0 baseline exists.
rationale: PF-3 passed as the load-bearing kill-test; the deferred sections were explicitly calibrated against data PF-0 had not produced yet.
alternatives_considered: build all four sections against a synthetic baseline
author: wes

decision: Fix three real lib/bench.py bugs found while gathering a third PF-0 data point, rather than working around them.
rationale: cargo 1.88.0 exits 101 (not 127) on an unrecognized subcommand; the nextest-missing fallback never fired until this was fixed.
alternatives_considered: special-case the new exit code at the call site instead of fixing bench.py
author: wes

decision: Extend konjo-ast-diff-rs with a --items mode using real syn spans, rather than falling back to an outcomes.json-derived approximation.
rationale: confirmed with a minimal scratch crate that span-locations gives real 1-indexed LineColumn values before touching the real crate.
alternatives_considered: use the outcomes.json-derived fallback line-number approximation
author: wes

decision: Scope --in-diff against the fixed production diff (diff_base_ref), separate from the round's own worktree checkout point (base_ref).
rationale: scoping --in-diff against a round's own test-writing diff touches zero production lines, so the loop would never find a single mutant; found by actually running the loop, not by inspection.
alternatives_considered: scope --in-diff against the round's own diff and accept the loop never finding mutants
author: wes

decision: Package konjo/mutation-hunt as a skill pointing at bin/kiban-mutation-hunt, with lopi's CI job opt-in via workflow_dispatch only.
rationale: the plan's own non-goal is no new default gate this sprint, and the loop spends real model tokens per round, so it should not run on every push.
alternatives_considered: wire it into the required push-triggered gate set immediately
author: wes

decision: Treat the task-to-diff harness as a permanent, one-way measurement instrument for every future authoring-context claim, not a one-off script.
rationale: Phase 2's six candidate invariants (and every later claim) now measure against this harness; reverting it invalidates the measurement basis those claims rest on.
alternatives_considered: treat it as disposable, throwaway tooling for this phase only
author: wes

decision: Add a tier field (blocking/advisory) to the profile schema, with the pre-existing advisory: bool flags kept working as aliases.
rationale: companion to lopi's own Gate-Tiering-1, so the BLOCKING/ADVISORY split does not have to be independently rediscovered per repo.
alternatives_considered: drop the legacy advisory: bool flags outright instead of aliasing them
author: wes

decision: Measure what a gate costs, not just what it catches, via gate_stats.py's BLOCKING_READY/ADVISORY_ONLY/INSUFFICIENT_DATA tags against a 5% false-positive ceiling over a 20-run floor.
rationale: the framework already measured whether a gate catches a defect; it never measured cost, and promoting a gate needs both a passing kill-test and a measured false-positive rate.
alternatives_considered: promote gates on kill-test results alone, without a cost measurement
author: wes

decision: Add gate_blocking_promotion as its own meta-gate rather than folding the check into gate_can_fail's existing blanket rule.
rationale: deliberately narrower -- the tier-specific half of the two promotion criteria -- so it survives independent of whether gate_can_fail's rule ever loosens for advisory-tier entries.
alternatives_considered: extend gate_can_fail's existing rule to cover tier promotion too
author: wes

decision: Ship gate_claude_contract as advisory across every pilot repo.
rationale: made S13 Phase 0's one-time hand audit of CLAUDE.md permanent and mechanical, starting from the same adoption-ramp shape as gate_polarity.
author: wes

decision: Flip gate_claude_contract to blocking for lopi (0 standing violations); keep squish and vectro advisory.
rationale: a default change made per-repo on measured evidence, not a blanket flip -- Phase 4 measured check_contract against all three real pilot repos' actual current CLAUDE.md.
alternatives_considered: flip all three repos to blocking at once
author: wes

decision: Sprint completion checklist requires a self-graded 'zero dead code' line.
rationale: original checklist wording; no independently verifiable command backed it.
author: wes

decision: Remove the self-graded 'zero dead code' checklist line and replace it with two concrete commands.
rationale: self-grading zero dead code produced no evidence a reviewer could check; kiban ships from one global clone, so replacing the line changes every consuming repo's definition of done simultaneously.
alternatives_considered: keep the self-graded line and add commands alongside it
author: wes

decision: review_diff defaults to runs=1 -- one pass per PR.
rationale: initial implementation default, never revisited after multi-run machinery was built.
author: wes

decision: Default review_diff to runs=3 instead of runs=1.
rationale: one pass was not enough for the single most consequential judgment in the framework; runs=1 was a leftover default nobody had revisited.
alternatives_considered: keep runs=1
make it repo-configurable only
author: wes

decision: If real syn spans don't work, fall back to an outcomes.json-derived line-number approximation for --items.
rationale: PF-1b's own stop rule named this as the fallback path if span-locations proved unusable.
author: wes

reason: confirmed span-locations gives real 1-indexed LineColumn values against a known 5-line snippet; the fallback was not needed.
author: wes

decision: Attempt to mechanically classify raw_index_external_input the same way as the other seven defect taxonomy classes.
rationale: taxonomy completeness goal for evals/genfixtures.py's MECHANICALLY_CLASSIFIED coverage.
author: wes

reason: confirmed genuinely not mechanically classifiable this way; recorded honestly as a gap rather than forced.
author: wes
